questions.question: What are CrewAI's four primitives?
options: Agent, Task, Crew, Process
Node, Edge, Reducer, Checkpointer
Actor, Message, Inbox, Runtime
Tool, Prompt, Model, Memory
questions.explanation: Agent, Task, Crew, and Process are the four primitives.

questions.question: What is the recommended production starting point per the CrewAI docs?
options: Crew, because LLM-driven autonomy is easiest to audit in production
Flow, because Crews are folded in only once autonomy earns its cost
Sequential process, because task order is fixed and predictable
Hierarchical process, because a manager Agent decides everything
questions.explanation: The docs say start production apps with Flows; fold Crews in as sub-steps when autonomy earns its cost.

questions.question: What is the difference between a Crew and a Flow?
options: Crew requires a paid CrewAI Enterprise license; Flow ships free in the open-source package
Crew requires GPU-backed inference for the manager Agent's routing calls; Flow runs on CPU only
Crew is autonomous and LLM-driven; Flow is event-driven, code-owned, deterministic and testable
Flow contains no Agents at all; only a Crew may define agents or call an LLM directly
questions.explanation: Crew is autonomy-first; Flow is determinism-first.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the four memory types CrewAI ships?
options: Short-term memory, a conversation buffer wiped at the end of the run
Long-term memory, persisted across runs in a vector DB
Entity memory, per-entity facts keyed by entity, not by similarity
Quantized memory, bit-packed embeddings compressed for storage
questions.explanation: Short-term, long-term, entity, and contextual are the four. Quantized memory is not a CrewAI concept.

questions.question: What is backstory bloat and how does the lesson recommend handling it?
options: 2000-word agent backstories push out the context budget; keep backstories under 200 words
Storing too many finished Crew definitions in one project file; archive the completed ones
Registering too many BaseTool subclasses on a single Agent; delete the unused tools
Bedrock inference calls running slow under sustained load; switch to a closer AWS region
questions.explanation: Backstories shape tone and judgment but eat context if oversized.

questions.question: When is Hierarchical process worth picking over Sequential?
options: Always, since Hierarchical is CrewAI's documented default process for every Crew
When you have 4+ specialists that need a manager Agent to route between them
When you have exactly one task and no need for any routing at all
When you do not have any tools registered on the specialist agents
questions.explanation: Hierarchical adds a manager Agent; only worthwhile when several specialists need dynamic routing.
